rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Ammonia is the lone pair with a résumé. **Pyramidal, sp³, 107°**, with bp −33 °C and a refrigerant-grade latent heat of 1370 kJ/kg, it donates that pair to H⁺ (alkaline solution, fountain experiment, red-litmus-blue), to HCl vapour (the white NH₄Cl fumes of the rod-and-bottle test), and to Cu²⁺ — where the NEB checklist unfolds in two acts: **CuSO₄ + 2NH₄OH → Cu(OH)₂↓** (pale blue) then **Cu(OH)₂ + 4NH₃ →…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Gas That Feeds and Chokes Ammonia is nitrogen's most useful compound — fertiliser feedstock, refrigerant, laboratory base — and its chemistry with CuSO₄, water, FeCl₃, concentrated HCl, mercurous nitrate paper and oxygen is a standard NEB checklist. This topic runs the reaction list, then weighs its applications against its hazards.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Preparation and structure - **Laboratory:** heating an ammonium salt with an alkali: 2NH₄Cl + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCl₂ + 2H₂O + 2NH₃ (dried over quicklime CaO — never conc. H₂SO₄, which absorbs it). - **Industrial (Haber):** N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, 450 °C, 200 atm, Fe catalyst.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: CuSO4 ladder: pale-blue ppt -> deep-blue solution in excess (complex); Fe stays brown. Dry NH3 over CaO only. White fumes = NH4Cl. Two O2 equations: no catalyst -> N2; Pt -> NO. Fridge numbers: -33 C bp, 1370 kJ/kg.

Explain with an equation.** — The rod releases **ammonia vapour** and the bottle releases **hydrogen chloride vapour**; where the two gases meet they combine directly…

rows.text: In reaction-list answers, state the observation AND the equation — NEB awards them separately; "deep blue solution in excess" is the copper-specific phrase.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: One lone pair runs ammonia's chemistry: it grabs H⁺ (basicity), grabs Cu²⁺ (the deep-blue complex), and hydrogen-bonds to itself (the anomalously high boiling point and the refrigerant-grade latent heat).

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Preparation: 2NH4Cl + Ca(OH)2 -> CaCl2 + 2H2O + 2NH3 (dry over CaO only); Haber: N2 + 3H2 = 2NH3 at 450 C/200 atm/Fe. Structure: pyramidal sp3, lone pair, angle 107, bp -33 C, latent heat 1370 kJ/kg.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Roughly 180 million tonnes of ammonia are made yearly — most of the world's nitrogen atoms in food passed through a Haber reactor first.

rows.text: Give the two ammonia-oxygen equations with their conditions.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **Excess reagent matters:** with CuSO₄, "blue precipitate" is only half the story — the deep-blue *solution* in excess NH₄OH is the observation that earns the complex-ion mark.  ·  **Drying agent choice:** drying NH₃ over conc. H₂SO₄ or CaCl₂ destroys it (both absorb it); only **quicklime CaO** works — a permanent NEB trap.
